page.layout: One page of text in running prose, with a centred closing prayer at its foot. Marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text a printed fleuron (ornament), then the signature at the foot.

l.i: libertatem philosophicam amant, eâq; veluti clypeo
muniti, ingrediuntur silvam philosophicam in primo
limine, in quo varia lustra, fera indomita, & aves
rapaces, tenebricosam; sed in penetra[illegible, ~1 letter]bus clarissimam,
ubi animalia amicabilia, arbores elegantula, fructus
visuntur. Adeste ergo, qui satagitis pugnare

main_text.l: CONFUSIONEM, quæ oberrant in hac, quam dixi
TEM, ORDINEM. Adeste, inquam, & hoc filo
Ariadneo utimini in cæco illo labyrintho. Pau-
cis enim vobis ostendam rectam cynosuram

l.i: & manuductionem, quam secuti non aberrabitis, ut est
in proverbio, à janua. Tu vero, Domine Deus,
pater cœlestis, da mihi recta scribere,
tibi in honorem, aliis in fructum.

marginalia.note: Tria mon-stra, contra quaedimicare debet literarum alumnus.

page.notes: Printed fleuron (ornament) below the text, not transcribed. The Greek-free text has no doubtful words except the following. "eâq;" is printed with a small superscript mark after the q that I could not read with certainty; it is copied as "eâq;" and should be checked. The word in "penetra..bus" has a damaged letter where a single letter (probably l) should be; it is marked illegible. The note "quaedimicare" is printed with a hyphen split as "quaedimica-re" and is copied whole. Long s in the notes ("monstra") is written as plain s. The printed "ut est" is copied as "ut est". Running head and page number are printed at the top. Signature "A 2" is at the foot.
